{{short description|French mathematician and publisher (1857–1945)}}
[[File:"Dodécaèdre régulier de 3e espèce à faces étoilées".jpg|thumb|"{{lang|fr|Dodécaèdre régulier de 3e espèce à faces étoilées}}" (likely a [[great icosahedron]]) from Vuibert's {{lang|fr|Les Anaglyphes geometriques}}, meant to be viewed with what are now called [[3-D glasses]] ]]
'''Désiré-Henry Vuibert''' (21 August 1857{{snd}}27 November 1945) was a French mathematician and publisher of technical books and journals, and founder of the French publishing house {{ill|Vuibert|fr}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Henry Vuibert (1857-1945) |url=https://data.bnf.fr/10338225/henry_vuibert/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=data.bnf.fr |language=fr |archive-date=2023-10-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031074941/https://data.bnf.fr/10338225/henry_vuibert/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Editions Vuibert |url=https://www.babelio.com/auteur/Editions-Vuibert/471466 |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=Babelio |language=fr |archive-date=2021-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205121320/https://www.babelio.com/auteur/Editions-Vuibert/471466 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was a publisher of the same class as [[Louis Christophe François Hachette|Louis Hachette]] and [[Pierre Larousse]], and is said to have begun his company in 1876.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mollier |first=Jean-Yves |date=2007 |title=ÉDITER AU XIX e SIÈCLE |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23013926 |journal=Revue d'Histoire littéraire de la France |volume=107 |issue=4 |pages=771–790 |doi=10.3917/rhlf.074.0771 |jstor=23013926 |issn=0035-2411|url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{Rp|page=780}} 

His book ''Les Anaglyphes geometriques'' described "Vuibert's principle of anaglyphic vision" based on a "procedure invented by [[Louis Arthur Ducos du Hauron|Louis Ducos du Houron]], which consisted in printing, in superimposition, pairs of stereoscopic views, taken in complementary colors".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Clair |first=Jean |date=September 1978 |title=Opticeries |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/778648 |journal=October |volume=5 |pages=101–112 |doi=10.2307/778648|jstor=778648 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This book and the concepts therein are said to have "inspired [[Marcel Duchamp]]'s interest in [[anaglyph 3D|anaglyph]]s".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rare Books |first=Blackwell's |title=Twitter - 1172811942219702274 |url=https://twitter.com/blackwellrare/status/1172811942219702274 |website=Twitter/X |access-date=2024-03-22 |archive-date=2019-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914112735/https://twitter.com/blackwellrare/status/1172811942219702274 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Les Anaglyphes geometriques'' "set the standard" for representation of 3D in two dimensions and offered a "grand tour of shape" that influenced both artists and mathematicians alike.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Witt |first=Andrew |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8QlNEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Henry+Vuibert%22&pg=PA161 |title=Formulations: Architecture, Mathematics, Culture |date=2022-01-11 |publisher=MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-54300-2 |pages=161 |language=en}}</ref>

Also, according to one account, it was Vuibert, not [[Eutaris]], who first worked out what is now called a [[Taylor circle]].<ref>{{Cite journal |year=1895 |title=REPONSES. |url=https://ttu-ir.tdl.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/b191af2b-d2fe-48ad-aa48-12f2bb5eac22/content |journal=[[L'Intermédiaire des mathématiciens]] |volume=II |page=166 |language=fr |via=[[Texas Tech|Texas Tech University Libraries]]}}</ref>
